quote.text: “What has been will be again, what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.”
quote.author: Ecclesiastes 1:9 (King James Version, 1611)

stories.kicker: Ukraine · The truce that travelled home with the plane
stories.headline: A pause, then the missiles again
stories.dek: The two-capital ceasefire that let two US envoys shuttle Moscow and Kyiv expired on Monday night. Within hours Russia hit Kyiv with one of its heaviest barrages of the war. The delta on last week’s “pause, not peace” is that the pause is now over.

stories.kicker: The regime · A hot number reopens the hike
stories.headline: The Fed’s hold, in question
stories.dek: One payroll report, wildly over forecast, did what a fortnight of Fed-speak could not — put a September rate rise back in the frame. Friday’s inflation reading throws the switch. Higher-for-longer has come back, and this time it answers to the word “hike.”

stories.kicker: Down the rabbit hole · Every console, in a jacket pocket
stories.headline: The hunt for the whole arcade
stories.dek: Somewhere between a fifty-dollar toy and a thousand-dollar Windows machine sits a fast-growing hobby: dedicated handhelds that emulate every console ever made. The gateway is cheap. The rabbit hole is not.

stories.kicker: The payout · Relief in the account, haze in the air
stories.headline: The money lands; the sky does not clear
stories.dek: The Cost-of-Living Special Payment starts hitting bank accounts today, four to six hundred dollars to more than two million adults. Overhead, the haze that first broke a hundred on the PSI last week refuses to fully lift.

stories.kicker: Buy it once · The bench that outlasts the knives
stories.headline: The edge, from the grit up
stories.dek: Sharpening is the rare category where the tool outlives everything it touches. A fifty-dollar stone and an eighty-dollar flattener will see out every knife in the drawer. Here is the hierarchy, taught from the abrasive up — and the point past which the spending is theatre.

stories.kicker: Chips · The loophole with a new name
stories.headline: The blacklist that changed its letterhead
stories.dek: A New York Times investigation says billions in banned Blackwell servers reached Chinese customers through a California firm that is a sanctioned company under a different name. It lands three weeks before Xi flies to the White House.

stories.kicker: The wrist · Motorola comes back, a beat late
stories.headline: A good watch, one chip generation behind
stories.dek: The Moto Watch Ultra is Motorola’s first serious Wear OS watch and its first with an LTE eSIM: a bright screen, two-day battery and Polar-grade training data. The catch a buy-once reader will feel is the silicon — a 2022 processor on last year’s software.

stories.kicker: Geneva · A small maker fixes a hundred-year-old flaw
stories.headline: The worldtimer that springs forward
stories.dek: MING’s 57.05 Comet does the thing the worldtimer has never done: it accounts for daylight saving. A single fifteen-degree click advances only the cities that change their clocks. Two hundred pieces, and it will be gone.

stories.kicker: Venice · The ovations, ahead of the verdict
stories.headline: Standing, and standing, and standing
stories.dek: The 83rd Venice Film Festival runs to Saturday, so the Golden Lion is still in its cage. But two films have turned their premieres into the longest ovations of the festival — and in Venice, that is usually the tell.

stories.kicker: The panel · Fix the features, not the birthday
stories.headline: The design, not the age on the box
stories.dek: Singapore’s expert panel has come down against a blanket social-media age ban and for regulating the addictive machinery — infinite scroll, autoplay, algorithmic feeds, visible like-counts. For a household with a twelve-year-old, it is the more useful conclusion. (General guidance, not medical advice.)

stories.kicker: The long game · The case against Zone 2 as the whole answer
stories.headline: The easy-cardio gospel, questioned
stories.dek: For two years the longevity crowd has told you to spend most of your cardio in Zone 2. A big new review says that for a time-crunched mid-forties trainee, that may be the least efficient way to build the engine that matters. (General guidance, not medical advice.)

stories.kicker: What’s worth booking · The dated agenda
stories.headline: Book this week, plan the season
stories.dek: Two clocks start this week — a Bruno Mars pre-sale on Thursday, a Kyushu sumo on-sale close behind. Below them sits the season to plan, each line re-confirmed against its primary ticket page on 8 September.

stories.kicker: The Undercurrent · Japan learns a new verb: to cancel
stories.headline: The country that is cancelling the effort
stories.dek: It started with a woman announcing she was too tired to bathe. Two years on, “cancel-sphere” culture has spread across Japanese social media into forty varieties — and a trade magazine has named its 2026 form, the “hardship-cancel sphere,” the theme of the year. In the country that invented death-by-overwork, a generation is refusing to endure.
